chunks: And from him from Ali ibn Yaqteen who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) - regarding a man who forgot the glorification (tasbih) in his bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujood). He said, 'There is no harm in that.'
As for that which indicates that if he leaves it deliberately, then there is no prayer for him, is what he narrated:

key_terms.تَسْبِيحَة: Glorification (specifically the phrases said in ruku and sujud)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on forgetting or deliberately omitting the tasbih in ruku and sujud?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the distinction between *nasī* (forgetfulness) and *ta‘ammud* (deliberate omission) regarding the recommended glorifications (tasbihat) in ruku’ and sujud. While forgetting them does not invalidate the prayer, the Imam indicates that intentional neglect renders the prayer void, a ruling supported by the specific hadith cited in the text. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the spiritual integrity of prayer, where conscious disregard of sunnah acts can impact the validity of the worship.
